clue.text: Fuss surrounding criminal, one to be believed

indicators.note: surrounding says the word for fuss goes around the other two pieces

parts.note: a carry-on is British informal for a fuss or commotion
a convict is a criminal serving a sentence
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: There is a commotion around a crook, yet he is someone whose word should be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' wants to be an anagram signal; it is a plain noun here. A carry-on is British informal for a fuss, and 'surrounding' wraps it round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: an argument that persuades its hearers is one that is able to be believed.

clue.text: Long to support cold store

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so the word for long comes after cold

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: A lengthy thing is needed to prop up a refrigerated storeroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' reads as an adjective of length but is the verb meaning to yearn. 'to support' places it below C in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a hidden stock of supplies or a hoard is a store.

clue.text: Gather fruit comes again

parts.note: to reap a crop is to gather it in
pears are fruit, the word serving as a plural

explanation.surface: At harvest time the picking season returns once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: whatever returns into view shows up a second time.

clue.text: Truck turned over in American garden

indicators.note: turned over tells you the word for truck is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a dray is a low cart or truck for heavy loads such as beer barrels

explanation.surface: A lorry has flipped onto its roof on a lawn in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' makes DRAY read from bottom to top. Americans use this word for the plot behind a house that the British call a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional usage: in the United States the lawn behind a house goes by this name.

clue.text: Dark yellow and green initially dividing a couple of veterans

indicators.note: dividing says the single letter sits between the two matching words and separates them
a couple of means the word for veteran is used twice over

parts.note: veteran as an adjective means old, as in a veteran car

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of green

explanation.surface: A paint scheme has a green stripe separating two elderly ex-soldiers from one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of' doubles OLD and 'dividing' drops the G of 'green initially' between the two copies.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour name: this is a dull brownish shade of yellow in paint and fabric charts.

clue.text: Leaves from tea scattered during holidays

indicators.note: during places the jumbled letters within the span of the word for holidays

parts.note: vacs is the university abbreviation for vacations

indicators.note: scattered things are thrown about, so the letters of tea are rearranged

explanation.surface: Loose tea foliage got strewn about while the family was away on a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' poses as tea leaves but is the verb meaning departs. 'scattered' gives ATE, which 'during' places inside the university shortening of vacations.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: someone who quits a room or post empties it.

clue.text: Charlie and heather laughing quietly

parts.note: Chuck is a familiar form of Charles, as Charlie is
ling is the common heather of British moors

explanation.surface: Two friends, Charlie and Heather, share a soft private giggle.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather is not a girl here but the moorland plant, also called ling.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a soft, suppressed giggle to oneself is exactly this.

clue.text: One apple drink lacking depth is rather cold

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: lacking says the word for the drink goes without one of its letters

parts.note: cider is the drink made from fermented apples
D is the abbreviation for depth in measurements

explanation.surface: A single apple drink without much body has been served a bit too chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparative: 'rather' gives the sense of somewhat more frosty than before.

clue.text: It's routine working in royal mint

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are operating in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A job making coins at the Royal Mint is just the daily grind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' is the anagram signal for ROYAL MINT. The Royal Mint is the British state's coin maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a noun: the usual, expected state of affairs is the daily round.

clue.text: Heard vegetable burnt

indicators.note: heard says the vegetable's name is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable with thick stalks

explanation.surface: Someone caught the sizzle of the greens scorching in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' is the homophone signal: CHARD, the leafy vegetable, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something scorched black by fire has been blackened in this way.

clue.text: Type of guide for tourists

definitions.meaning: a well-known typewriter-style typeface carries this name
a person employed by a travel company to accompany and assist holidaymakers

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a monospaced font, and a travel firm's escort for holidaymakers.

clue.text: Spot a reversal in Tory psephology

indicators.note: reversal says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An analyst notices a turnaround in the Conservatives' election statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversal' reads YPSE backwards and 'in' shows it lies inside the two words. Psephology is the study of elections.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to catch sight of or notice something.

clue.text: Country that's OK? No, rather troubled

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of the three words before it are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asked whether a nation is all right, someone answers that it is in quite a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' is the anagram signal for OK, NO and RATHER together.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a state on the peninsula east of China.

clue.text: Broke right away and landed ashore

indicators.note: away says the letter for right departs from the word for broke

parts.note: to breach a rule or a wall is to break it

explanation.surface: A penniless man ran off at once and came ashore somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broke' reads as penniless but is the past tense of break. 'away' takes R out of BREACHED.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a boat or whale run up onto the sand has come to rest on the shore.

clue.text: Black whole nuts are in pavlova?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the whole of something is all of it

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the two words after it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A meringue dessert turns out to contain dark, uncrushed nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pavlova' reads as the dessert but points to Anna Pavlova, the dancer it was named after. 'nuts' turns ARE IN into ERINA.
explanation.definitionFit: An example, flagged by the question mark: Anna Pavlova was a celebrated Russian dancer.

clue.text: Tricky issue for Jersey?

definitions.meaning: a controversial matter nobody wants to handle
a Jersey Royal is a British new spud, here pictured warm from the pan; a jersey also keeps you warm

explanation.definitionFit: Two readings of one phrase: an awkward controversial matter, and whimsically a cooked Jersey Royal spud.

clue.text: Spurs ground limits restricting united

indicators.note: restricting says the rearranged letters hem in the single letter
ground as the past of grind means the letters of limits are milled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, six letters to rearrange
U is the abbreviation for united, as in Man U

explanation.surface: Tottenham's stadium boundaries are cramping Manchester United's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spurs' looks like the London football club and 'ground' its stadium. 'ground' turns LIMITS into STIMLI, and 'restricting' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a plural noun: things that prompt or goad a response.

clue.text: Preposterous hunt relay attacked

indicators.note: attacked suggests the letters are set upon and knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An absurd incident in which a team race for huntsmen was set upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attacked' is the anagram signal for HUNT RELAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal sense: an absurdly early or unreasonable hour is called this.

clue.text: Look to protect those travelling in the country

indicators.note: to protect says the word for look shelters the jumbled letters within it

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters of those are moving about

parts.note: taken as written, five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Keep watch to safeguard the people journeying through the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' reads as the countryside but means a nation. 'travelling' gives ESOTH, which 'to protect' places inside the old exclamation for look.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is a kingdom wholly enclosed by South Africa.

clue.text: March maybe leaving front, say — nothing very active

indicators.note: leaving front says the word for what March exemplifies loses its opening letter

parts.note: March is an example of a month
eg means for example, as say does
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Troops marching away from the front line are, supposedly, not at all busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like soldiers marching but is the calendar month. 'leaving front' drops M from MONTH, leaving ONTH.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone constantly busy and moving about is described this way.

clue.text: Wife smothering Jack in sugar leads to jocularity

indicators.note: smothering says wife covers over and blots out Jack, taking his place

parts.note: jaggery is a coarse dark sugar made from palm sap
J is the abbreviation for the jack in cards

explanation.surface: A wife covering her husband Jack in sugar ends in general merriment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smothering' has W cover up the J 'in sugar', JAGGERY, so W replaces J.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: playful joking and mischievous humour.

clue.text: Conflict in Washington about keeping some distance

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state

indicators.note: keeping says the word for about holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: re means about or concerning
something some distance off is far

explanation.surface: A dispute in the American capital over staying well apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: armed fighting between nations or groups.

clue.text: Free y-fronts cut badly showing lots of cheek

indicators.note: badly says the letters are poorly arranged and need reordering

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: cut says y-fronts is shortened by losing its final letter

explanation.surface: Complimentary men's briefs, poorly tailored, reveal a good deal of buttock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims the S from Y-FRONTS and 'badly' rearranges FREE with YFRONT. Y-fronts are British men's briefs, so 'cheek' looks bodily but means impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: barefaced impudence is a great deal of nerve.

clue.text: Impose before anyone else, as comic mason would say

indicators.note: the word is spoken in the New York accent of the comedian Jackie Mason, which changes its vowel

parts.note: whoever arrives before anyone else is first

explanation.surface: A joking stonemason claims the right to lay down the rules ahead of everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic mason' is Jackie Mason, the New York comedian, in whose accent FIRST comes out as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to force something unwanted on somebody.

clue.text: Polish going after good food

indicators.note: going after says the word for polish follows the letter for good

parts.note: to polish something is to rub it

explanation.surface: A Pole goes in search of a decent meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised to look like the nationality but is the verb meaning to shine.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang synonym: informal word for something to eat.

clue.text: Herb, a serially chaotic character

definitions.meaning: an aromatic kitchen plant used in pesto
Mr Fawlty, the frantic hotelier of the British TV sitcom series Fawlty Towers

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one name: a pesto plant, and the hapless hotelier Fawlty in a British sitcom series.

clue.text: Storyteller in bar on the way up

indicators.note: in a down clue, on the way up means the word for bar is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rail is a horizontal bar

explanation.surface: A raconteur holds forth in a pub further along the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' reads RAIL from the bottom of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism: someone who tells stories is a teller of untruths.

clue.text: Leaders missing, check overdue copy

indicators.note: leaders missing says each of the two words that follow loses its opening letter

parts.note: to check something is to limit or restrain it
something overdue is late

explanation.surface: With the editors absent, someone must chase up an article that is behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders missing' removes the opening L from both LIMIT and LATE, leaving IMIT and ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to mimic or reproduce something.

clue.text: A spot perhaps close to grass lands

parts.note: a spot, short for spotlight, is one kind of light

indicators.note: close to means the end of the word grass, its final letter

explanation.surface: A patch of ground, possibly next to some pasture and fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lands' looks like a noun for terrain but is the verb. 'close to' takes the last letter of GRASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: a bird that comes down and settles does this.

clue.text: Early star or moon will excite one

indicators.note: will excite says the preceding words are stirred into motion, their letters agitated

parts.note: taken as written, fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The first star of evening, or the moon, is bound to thrill a certain person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will excite' is the anagram signal for EARLY STAR OR MOON. The whole clue describes 'one': Britain's senior official stargazer, an honorary post in the royal household.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the holder of this British court post is a person whom heavenly bodies thrill.
